# 3. gtr.json and the generated files

## gtr.json

`gtr.json` is the only file you edit by hand. The full field list is in the
[reference](../reference/gtr-json.md); a typical application:

```json
{
    "$schema": "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shibisty/gtr/main/schema/gtr.schema.json",
    "name": "blog",
    "version": "1.0.0",
    "private": true,
    "engines": { "go": ">=1.22", "gtr": "^0.2" },
    "dependencies": {
        "orm": "github:shibisty/orm.go#^0.2",
        "orm-postgres": "github:shibisty/orm.go-postgres-driver#^0.1",
        "github.com/google/uuid": "^1.6"
    },
    "devDependencies": {
        "faker": "github:shibisty/faker.go#^0.1"
    },
    "scripts": {
        "start": "go run .",
        "test": "go test ./...",
        "migrate": "go run . migrate"
    }
}
```

- **`name`** is the import path of the project's own packages: `import "blog/internal/posts"`.
- **`engines.go`** decides which Go runs the project and the `go` line of `go.mod`;
  **`engines.gtr`** which gtr-manager. Both are ranges ([Go versions](07-go-versions.md)).
- **`dependencies`** are keyed by import path, valued by where the package comes from:
  `import "orm"`, `import postgres "orm-postgres"`, `import "github.com/google/uuid"`.
- **`devDependencies`** are for tests and tools; an application that depends on your
  package does not get them.
- **`private: true`** stops `gtr publish` — for applications.
- **`$schema`** gives editors completion and checks (VS Code, GoLand).

## What gtr writes

| File | What it is | Commit? |
|---|---|---|
| `gtr.lock` | the exact version, source, commit and hash of every package | **yes** |
| `go.mod` | generated from `gtr.json` for the go command and editors | no (in `.gitignore`) |
| `go.work` | in a [workspace](08-workspaces.md) root: the members | no |
| `gtr_modules/` | links to the packages in `~/.gtr/store` | no |
| `node_modules/` | npm packages, when `gtr.json` has `npm:` dependencies | no |
| `.gtr/links.json` | your [local copies](08-workspaces.md#local-copies) of packages | no |

`gtr.lock` is what makes installs repeatable: `gtr install` keeps the versions in it, and
`gtr ci` installs exactly them and fails when they no longer match `gtr.json`.

### go.mod

```
// generated by gtr from gtr.json — edit gtr.json or run `gtr sync`
// gtr:hash sha256:5bc5…

module blog

go 1.22

require orm v0.2.1

replace orm => ./gtr_modules/orm
…
```

Every package is a `require` with a `replace` into `gtr_modules/`, so the go command finds
everything locally and never downloads (gtr runs it with `GOPROXY=off`). Do not edit the
file: the first line carries a hash, and gtr refuses to overwrite a changed `go.mod`.
If you did edit it (or ran `go get`), `gtr sync` carries the change over into `gtr.json`;
`gtr sync --force` throws it away. `go mod tidy` leaves it as it is.

If you want `go.mod` in the repository anyway (so that `go install` works on the project
without gtr), set `"gomod": "commit"`.

### The store

Downloaded packages live in `~/.gtr/store` once per version and are shared by all your
projects; `gtr_modules/` only links to them (junctions on Windows, so no administrator
rights are needed). A stored package is never changed: `gtr ci` re-hashes it and stops if a
file under `gtr_modules/` was edited. Delete `gtr_modules/` whenever you like —
`gtr install` brings it back without downloading.
